newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 16.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning.
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Low volumes seen as Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and some regional bourses remain closed for local religious festival, traders say. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) will be open for trade. All commodities markets and banks also shut in Bombay
** Indian stock markets expected to slide this week on fears of economic slowdown and sluggish growth in corporate earnings, brokers and analysts say

Last week, Bombay's benchmark 30-share index slumped 160.70 points or 4.8 percent to 3347.37 after the government failed to deliver anticipated tax reliefs, including a waiver of a minimum corporate tax proposed in the government's July budget
** The government of the eastern Indian state of Orissa on Saturday hands over management of power distribution in central parts of the state to a private company, BSES Ltd, officials say
Orissa has become the first state to undertake a major step under India's economic reform programme launched in 1991 to restructure its state-run electricity distribution services
** Unit Trust of India decides to set up a dedicated debt fund overseas with an initial corpus of $100 million, the Business Standard newspaper reports
** The BSE falls to third place in terms of turnover during 1995/96 (April-March) with the NSE in the top spot and the Calcutta bourse coming in second, the Financial Express newspaper reports
** A sharp drop in the price of the BSE broking card is inducing firms from regional exchanges to seek membership on the Bombay bourse, the Economic Times newspaper reports
** Indian companies are likely to boost their earnings next year as global commodity prices improve, securities firm James Capel B&K says in a report
"While earnings growth will slow to 11 percent in FY97, we are forecasting a 23 percent growth in FY98 (1997/98 April-March)," the firm says
MARKETS:
** On Friday, the 30-share BSE index closed 44.17 points or 1.3 percent lower at 3347.37
** The 100-share National index fell 14.45 points or 0.95 percent to 1512.42
STOCKS TO WATCH:

** Leading hospitality firm Indian Hotels Company seeks shareholder approval to raise upto 231 million rupees through two term loans to part-finance hotel projects in the western state of Rajasthan. The company's annual shareholders' meeting is scheduled to be held on September 24 in Bombay, its annual report says

** A sharp slowdown in the sales of light commercial vehicles -- a segment dominated by TELCO, Ashok Leyland and Bajaj Tempo -- has led to a significant piling up of stock with dealers, the Economic Times reports

** The finance ministry may prune the size of State Bank of India's GDR offering due to poor credit offtake and the low price of the underlying share, the Business Standard reports. Pre-marketing for the $400 million SBI issue is due to begin this week
** Premier Automobiles is likely to introduce its 1700 cc diesel-driven Uno model in early 1997, the Financial Express reports
